messages:
Priya: Heads-up — a customer filed a ticket saying long-running Python generations (30-45s) started failing after they upgraded to our SDK v0.9.1. They see ConnectionResetError or 'stream closed' midway through token streaming.

Devon: Do we have their snippet and which timeout flags they set? The python client maps to httpx timeouts so there are a bunch of places to misconfigure.

Priya: Here's the minimal snippet they sent:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout=60)
resp = client.generate(model='rw-v1', prompt='long prompt...', max_tokens=1200)
print(resp.text)
```
They thought timeout=60 would cover long generations.

James: Ah — important detail: in v0.9.x we changed the public param name from `timeout` to `request_timeout` to avoid clashing with lower-level transport timeouts. If customers pass `timeout=60` it will be ignored on the new client constructor and fallback to the httpx default (which can be 10s for some paths) — that will cause mid-stream resets.

Priya: That's probably it. The ticket didn't mention any warnings, just the stack: `httpx.RemoteProtocolError: Connection reset by peer` plus `ConnectionError` from our streaming iterator.

Devon: Recommend these immediate troubleshooting steps we can ask them to try:
• Upgrade/downgrade to a pinned SDK that matches semantics (v0.9.1 expects `request_timeout`).
• Try explicit httpx-style timeout object via `client = RedwoodClient(..., request_timeout=httpx.Timeout(60.0))` if they use httpx.
• If streaming, set longer `request_timeout` and also ensure `stream=True` usage matches our streaming examples.

Priya: Added to reply draft. Quick question — is there also a separate connect/read/write mapping we should call out? They asked about connect/read/write vs a single global timeout.

James: Yes — httpx exposes connect/read/write/pool timeouts via `httpx.Timeout(connect=5.0, read=60.0, write=60.0)`. Our higher-level `request_timeout` is a convenience that sets reasonable defaults but can be overridden by passing an explicit `transport_timeout`/`httpx.Timeout` in the client config. We didn't document that clearly in the changelog for 0.9.0 — that's on us.

Priya: I'll include an explicit example for the support reply showing how to set both a high read timeout and a long overall request timeout.

Devon: Also ask them to capture the SDK version + httpx version + python version. We saw one customer where httpx 0.24 changed connection pooling semantics and shortened default keepalive which contributed.

Priya: Good call. I'll ask for: `pip freeze | grep -E \"(redwood|httpx)\"` and a short repro script. If they can reproduce reliably we'll escalate to eng-runtime with the trace.

SupportBot: Reminder: link support ticket #5821 for follow-up and attach logs.

Priya: Reply sent with repro instructions and a suggested workaround (pin to v0.8.3 or set `request_timeout=httpx.Timeout(read=120.0)`). I'll update once they respond; flagging for docs update on the param rename and timeout guidance. :thumbsup:
